# Scene encoders: sparse-voxel networks

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">Seed-based · 5 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set backbone=</code><span class="gp-chip">8 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

These encoders quantise the cloud to a voxel grid they own and run sparse convolutions on the
occupied voxels, then hand every point the feature of its voxel. The grid edge, 5 mm in every
preset, is their unit of length. What all scene encoders share is on the
[overview](scene_encoders.md).

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set backbone=minkunet34c -o graspnet-baseline_minkunet34c.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list backbone
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=minkunet34c -o gsnet_minkunet34c.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set backbone=minkunet34c -o scale-balanced-grasp_minkunet34c.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list backbone
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=minkunet34c -o economicgrasp_minkunet34c.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set backbone=minkunet34c -o finegrasp_minkunet34c.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#backbone) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#backbone) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#backbone) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#backbone) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#backbone).

??? note "What the columns say, and who is left out"

    - **Runs**: out of the methods the option is a swap under, those under which its probe trained on real frames without error. A method that ships the option is named *own* and not counted; a method still undecided is counted and named. Measured on 20 training iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, one run per cell; nothing was measured on GraspClutter6D or on Kinect frames.
    - **Trains like shipped**: out of the methods under which the swap ran, those under which every comparable loss term ended within the method's tolerance of the component it ships, with nothing rising; a method left out is named with why. Measured on 250 iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, at a constant learning rate (FineGrasp: its own warm-up), beside the method as shipped trained the same way twice.
    - [How we measure](../evidence/index.md) defines every word of these columns.

    Who is left out, and why:

    - `oacnns`, runs: not GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp (unstable twice in the short probe).
    - `oacnns`, trains like shipped: not compared under GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp: the swap did not run at level 1.
    - `spunet`, trains like shipped: not compared under FineGrasp: the swap did not run at level 1.

## Choosing

- **The grid is the first thing to sweep.** 5 mm keeps the grid of the reference methods;
  weights from rooms were trained at 2 to 2.5 cm (`--opts model.backbone.voxel_size=0.01`).
- **Weights whose input is what the methods feed:** `minkunet18a-openscene` was trained on three
  constant ones per point, so its first layer loads too (not under FineGrasp, which feeds
  coordinates and normals).
- **Pre-training on single partial frames:** `minkunet34c-pointcontrast`, trained on pairs of
  RGB-D frames, the regime of one table-top view.
- **A permissive licence, self-supervised:** `spunet-gaussiancross` (MIT).
- **Deeper and pretrained encoders** usually want a lower rate and a warm-up than the recipes
  tuned for a 14-layer network; none of this was tuned here.

## Details

??? note "The settings that matter"

    ```yaml
    model:
      backbone:
        type: MinkUNet
        in_channels: 3            # what the method feeds; compose sets it
        out_channels: 512         # free 1x1 projection; null returns the decoder width
        voxel_size: 0.005         # the encoder's unit of length, in metres
        layers: [2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2]
        planes: [32, 64, 128, 256, 128, 128, 96, 96]
        stem_kernel: 5            # 5 in MinkUNet; 3 in the Res16UNet34C checkpoints
    ```

    `MinkUNet` is one class for the whole family of MinkowskiEngine; `layers`, `planes` and
    `block` select the member (only 18A and 34C have presets):

    | Member | `layers` | Decoder half of `planes` (the encoder half is 32, 64, 128, 256) | `block` |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | 14A / 14B / 14C / 14D | `[1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]` | 128-128-96-96 / 128-128-128-128 / 192-192-128-128 / 384-384-384-384 | `basic` |
    | 18A / 18B / 18D | `[2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2]` | as 14A / 14B / 14D | `basic` |
    | 34A / 34B / 34C | `[2, 3, 4, 6, 2, 2, 2, 2]` | 256-128-64-64 / 256-128-64-32 / 256-128-96-96 | `basic` |
    | 50 / 101 | 34's / `[2, 3, 4, 23, 2, 2, 2, 2]` | 256-128-96-96 | `bottleneck` |

    Sparse convolutions go through `grasppanda.ops.sparse` (spconv underneath; one `spconv`
    extra per CUDA build).

??? note "How released weights load"

    Name a release as `pretrained:` (table below) or give a file path:

    ```yaml
    model:
      backbone:
        type: SpUNet
        in_channels: 3
        out_channels: 512
        grid_size: 0.005
        pretrained: gaussiancross-scannet-lin   # a name, or a file path
        pretrained_mismatch: skip               # error (default): refuse any tensor that does not load
    ```

    - **Only the encoder is loaded.** The loader finds the prefix under which the file keeps it,
      ignores heads and optimiser state, and re-lays kernels where the original library stores
      them differently. No pickled code runs.
    - **`pretrained_mismatch: skip`** keeps the initialisation of the tensors that do not fit and
      lists them in the log. A grasp model nearly always needs it, for two layers: the stem
      (releases read colour and normals, the methods feed constant ones) and the final projection
      when `out_channels` differs.
    - **A grasp checkpoint still wants the released file**, because `pretrained` loads when the
      encoder is built. Keep the file, or set `pretrained: null` to evaluate a grasp checkpoint.
    - **Other files of the same releases** (the other GaussianCross models, the other Volt
      teachers, the other Mask3D checkpoints) have the same layout and are expected to load the
      same way; they were not downloaded. Pass such a file as a path, with the options the load
      report asks for.

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **The stem is the tensor that does not load**, and it reads the input. A 6-channel stem
      loads under FineGrasp, but nothing says its six channels mean what the release was trained
      on. Loading says nothing about meaning.
    - **Licences differ inside one family.** PointContrast, Mask3D and OpenScene publish code
      under MIT or Apache-2.0 and say nothing about the weights, which were trained on ScanNet.
    - **`SpUNet` is not `MinkUNet34C`.** Same block counts and widths, but the width changes in
      another layer; a checkpoint of one does not fit the other, and the loader says so rather
      than loading half of it.
    - **Two kernel sizes may not share a spconv indice key.** A 5³ stem sharing the key of the 3³
      blocks ran on the CPU and failed on the GPU; the stem of `MinkUNet` has its own key.
    - **Legacy-format checkpoints that pickle foreign objects** cannot be read without executing
      them and are refused; re-save the state dict where it was written.

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | Contrastive Scene Contexts, Res16UNet34C pre-training | a legacy pickle with objects of its code base; the reader refuses to execute it. |
    | FCAF3D / TR3D sparse backbones (MMDetection3D) | layers the sparse facade does not have, and they return a pyramid of coarse levels, not per-point features. |
    | SPVCNN / SPVNAS | runs on TorchSparse, a second sparse library with no backend here. |
    | PonderV2 `SpUNet-v1m3` | another module tree than `SpUNet`; needs a key map. Small follow-up. |
    | Mosaic3D SpUNet | no licence on the model card. |
    | OA-CNNs weights | none released; `oacnns` starts from random weights. |
